The manipulation of time in the story is very effective and well-balanced, serving the narrative's comedic and thematic needs. Because the story covers an entire academic year (from autumn to May) within a short story format, the author relies heavily on the **compression of time** to convey the exhausting, grinding nature of the construction project. Whole months—such as November ("By Thanksgiving"), February, and April—are summarized in single paragraphs to show the gradual degradation of the building and the faculty's morale. 

Conversely, the author slows the pace down—**stretching time** into real-time scenes—for specific, high-impact moments that illustrate the absurdity of the situation. For example, the moment the tar blister swells and bursts during Arthur's colloquium, and the sudden catastrophic flooding of the lounge in March, are given detailed, moment-by-moment descriptions. This balance allows the reader to feel the prolonged weariness of the year-long renovation while still enjoying the sharp, immediate comedy of its worst disasters.
